model.name: Learning Activity / Course Delivery
model.purpose: Represent one governed delivery aggregate for a bounded learning activity, course, class, cohort, self-paced offering, workshop or session, connecting immutable learning intent to actual instruction, participation evidence, assessment and bounded outcomes.
model.scope_statement: Owns delivery identity and lineage, mandatory delivery profile, exact course, activity, curriculum and objective bindings, delivery-scoped design, provider and role assignments, cohort and participation assertions, schedule, location and modality, resource and tool bindings, instruction, attendance and learning-event assertions, assessment administrations, progress and completion assertions, quality, lifecycle, interoperability, access and retention. Person, Learner, Organization, Programme, Course or Activity Definition, Competency, Academic Session, Location, Resource, Tool, Enrollment, Attendance, Assessment Definition, Submission, Assessment Result, Qualification, Credential, Dataset, Communication, Artifact and Audit masters remain external.
in_scope: Delivery identity, profile, lineage, provider, authority, curriculum, objectives, instructional design, roles, cohorts, enrollment bindings and access
Schedule, sessions, modality, locations, resources, tools, assignments, instruction, facilitation, attendance, participation and learning-experience events
Assessment administrations, result links, feedback, progress, mastery and completion assertions, quality, lifecycle, interoperability, privacy, retention and safe agents
out_of_scope: Independent person, learner, provider, programme, course or activity definition, competency, session, location, resource, tool, enrollment, attendance, assessment, submission, result, qualification, credential, communication, artifact or audit master lifecycles
Inferring enrollment from access, attendance from login, learning from activity completion, mastery from one score, qualification from course completion or causality from learning analytics
Implementing a student information system, learning management system, learning record store, assessment platform, content repository, credential wallet or universal education policy and legal regime

boundary_notes.neighbor: Course, Activity, Curriculum or Programme Definition
boundary_notes.distinction: Reusable intent, structure, prerequisites and objectives are external versioned definitions. The delivery binds exact revisions and records one governed realization.
The delivery owns source-qualified participation and role assertions. External identity and enrollment masters retain admission authority, lifecycle and learner rights.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Session, Attendance or Learning Experience Event
boundary_notes.distinction: These are planned or observed occurrences within the delivery. Source events keep their own actor, action, object, context, time, authority and voiding semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Assessment Definition, Submission, Result or Grade
boundary_notes.distinction: The delivery binds assessment revisions and issues delivery-scoped administration and grading assertions while external evidence and result masters retain identity and review history.

Completion or mastery can support a separately authorized achievement, credit, qualification or credential. The delivery cannot issue or own those records unless explicitly delegated by their master system.

functions.name: Register learning delivery

preconditions: identity, duplicate, profile, authority and boundary checks pass
effects: one delivery aggregate exists without copying the course definition, learner or programme

functions.name: Bind curriculum, objectives and design
functions.description: Freeze exact course or activity definitions, competency targets, prerequisites, pedagogy, sequence and success rules.
preconditions: versions, scope, outcomes, workload, dependencies, language and adaptation rules validate
effects: delivery intent remains interpretable after source definitions change

functions.name: Assign authority, roles and safeguards
functions.description: Bind provider, instructors, assessors, support roles, privacy rules and accessibility controls.
preconditions: authority, delegation, separation, privacy, accessibility and exception checks pass
effects: learning delivery can operate within an explicit control envelope

functions.name: Enroll, allocate and provision
functions.description: Record source-qualified learner and cohort relationships, eligibility, capacity, waitlist, access and accommodations.
preconditions: identity matching, eligibility, prerequisite, capacity, privacy and accommodation checks pass

functions.name: Schedule sessions and resources
functions.description: Publish and revise calendars, locations, modality, content, tools, activities and availability.
preconditions: time-zone, recurrence, rights, version, accessibility, dependency and capacity checks pass
effects: participants and systems can resolve what is available when and where

functions.name: Record instruction and participation
functions.description: Append actual sessions, facilitation, attendance and immutable learner-experience events without converting them into learning claims.
preconditions: actor, action, object, context, authority, time, privacy and voiding checks pass
effects: actual delivery history remains attributable and source-qualified

functions.name: Administer assessments and return feedback
functions.description: Bind exact assessment revisions, accept governed submissions and record results, grades, feedback and review lineage.
preconditions: attempt, accommodation, integrity, scale, assessor, evidence, moderation and appeal checks pass
effects: performance evidence remains distinct from mastery and qualification

functions.name: Evaluate progress, mastery and completion

preconditions: rule version, evidence, authority, uncertainty, contrary evidence and downstream-boundary checks pass

functions.name: Review, correct, repeat and improve
functions.description: Preserve released history while appending disputes, corrections, cancellations, improvements or a new repeat-delivery identity.
outputs: review event, correction successor, improvement action or new delivery root
preconditions: expected revision, reason, impact, affected scope and residual-validity checks pass
effects: later change cannot erase prior rosters, events, grades or outcomes

functions.name: Project, disclose, retain and audit

outputs: projection, disclosure, disposition or audit event
preconditions: mapping loss, privacy, redaction, hold, tombstone, idempotency and post-checks validate
effects: learning context remains interoperable, protected and accountable

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authoritative source plus delivery identifier, mandatory delivery profile and lineage head, not by course title, class code, dates, instructor or digest.

patch_rules: Extensions declare education sector and delivery profile, target finding, semantics, authority, lifecycle, accessibility, privacy, assessment, quality and interoperability effects.
Released rosters, schedules, events, submissions, results, grades and outcomes are immutable; corrections create attributable successors and repeat deliveries create new roots.
A patch must never silently change curriculum revision, objectives, eligibility, learner identity, accommodations, grading rule, source evidence or original event history.

artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate planned, effective, event, submission, assessment, result, release, ingestion and knowledge times and preserve source precision.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {delivery-id}--{release-or-session}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use title, class code, date, timestamp or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, delivery and release binding, source and profile versions, definition, resource, assessment and grading revisions, generating actor or tool, event and knowledge times, access marking and provenance.

policies: A Learning Activity or Course Delivery is not the reusable Course or Activity Definition, Curriculum or Programme, a Learner, Enrollment, Session, learning event, Assessment, Qualification or Credential.
Access, login, attendance, participation, engagement, learning, assessment success, mastery, completion, credit, qualification and credential remain separate source-qualified assertions.

Delivery ownership does not transfer ownership of person, learner, organization, programme, course, activity, competency, session, location, resource, tool, enrollment, attendance, assessment, submission, result, qualification, credential, communication, artifact or audit masters. Delivery disposition never cascades to linked masters.

Agents may validate, link and project allowlisted data, but enrollment admission, learner contact, accommodation decisions, grading, mastery or completion signoff, credential issuance, protected disclosure and disposition require delegated authority and applicable policies.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The model is a bounded delivery lifecycle container (aggregate root per domain-driven design) with explicit composition relations to external masters: person, learner, organization, programme, course, activity, competency, session, location, resource, tool, enrollment, assessment, submission, result, qualification, credential, communication and audit remain external. The delivery owns identity, mandatory profile, exact definition and objective revisions, provider authority, role assignments, enrollment participation assertions, schedule, resources, instruction, events, assessments, progress and completion within its scope, not the reusable definition, learner or master system lifecycles. Five boundary notes explicitly state distinctions from neighboring entities. Mandatory profile and external definition binding confirm aggregate boundary. The schema enum 'aggregate' is correct; a frozen registry value like 'standalone-mm' classifies the record plane and is never a valid subject-model entry kind.

decisions.rationale: Model correctly maps to schema enum 'aggregate'. It is a bounded delivery container with composition relations to external masters (learner, organization, course, assessment, credential), not a standalone entity. Mandatory profile and external definition binding confirm aggregate boundary. Five explicit boundary notes distinguish it from Course Definition, Person, Learner, Session, Assessment, Qualification and Credential masters. Domain-driven design and ownership rules support this classification.

decisions.concept: Learner and enrollment boundary: source-qualified assertions vs. external masters
decisions.rationale: Boundary is correctly drawn: learner and enrollment identity remain external; delivery records source-qualified participation assertions within its scope. Boundary notes explicitly distinguish 'External learner and cohort references' from 'source-qualified participation and role assertions' owned by delivery. However, data model should include explicit composition-relation artifact types (learner-reference, enrollment-reference) to enforce this at schema level, preventing accidental ownership collapse at implementation time. Accept boundary; require schema-level reinforcement.

decisions.concept: Source versioning, authority tier and specification maturity
decisions.rationale: All 16 sources pinned to versions or access dates (2026-09-06). Authority tier consistently 1 (primary sources). Standards bodies authoritative (UNESCO, EC, 1EdTech, W3C, IETF, NIST, ADL, UK National Archives). Coverage notes correctly identify Edu-API as Candidate Final Public (not released) and Common Cartridge 1.4 as Candidate Final. No conformance claim to final versions made, which is correct. Accept for reviewable-draft; final promotion requires final-version conformance or explicit specification-level hold declaration in publication artifacts.

decisions.concept: Inference safeguards: login, attendance, activity, learning, score, mastery, completion and qualification boundaries
decisions.disposition: Deferred: policy stated, schema enforcement absent
decisions.rationale: Adversarial checks and service-layer policies explicitly forbid collapsing: enrollment inferred from access, attendance from login, learning from activity completion, mastery from one score, qualification from completion. Policy is clear and strong. However, data model provides no technical schema elements (evidence-method tags, confidence markers, forbidden-rule validators, source-method requirements) to enforce or audit these distinctions at implementation time. Consumer implementation could still collapse them. Accept policy intent; defer with hold pending schema-level constraints that make distinctions machine-checkable.

decisions.concept: Interoperability: ISCED, ELM, Edu-API, OneRoster, Caliper, CASE, QTI, xAPI, CLR and CourseInstance crosswalk
decisions.disposition: Deferred: intent clear, working round-trip and conflict rules not proven
decisions.rationale: Model lists 11 mapping targets; crosswalk finding marked 'covered' in layer. However, coverage checklist explicitly shows 'composition' as gap; known omissions state 'proposed relations or mapping versions remain held for review.' No approved mapping tables, version-pair conflict rules or bidirectional proof supplied. OneRoster K-12 oriented, Edu-API higher-education oriented, ELM European; universal interoperability not formally claimed but variance not formally scoped. Accept intent; defer interoperability claim pending approved mapping tables with identified omissions, conflict-resolution rules for each standard pair and working round-trip tests.

Patch rules correctly enforce: 'Released rosters, schedules, events, submissions, results, grades and outcomes are immutable; corrections create attributable successors and repeat deliveries create new roots.' This prevents silent overwriting and preserves full history with attribution. Service-layer CRUD and adversarial checks reinforce. Accept. Technical constraint at schema level (forbidding PATCH on released artifacts, requiring POST for corrections with prior-reference) would strengthen confidence but is implementation detail.

decisions.concept: Accessibility, child protection, learner-rights and regional legal variance
decisions.disposition: Deferred: scope acknowledged and required, specialist review pending
decisions.rationale: Model references WCAG 2.2 (W3C Dec 2024) and coverage explicitly covers accessibility layer. However, known omissions and regional assumptions sections acknowledge that accessibility, child protection, learner consent, grading authority, retention rules and credential authority vary by jurisdiction and provider. Known omissions explicitly state 'education-sector, pedagogy, accessibility, learner-rights, analytics, regional and legal review is required before canonical promotion.' Accept acknowledgment; defer full scope pending education-sector review, accessibility conformance audit, child-protection governance mapping, and jurisdiction-specific policy coverage (FERPA, GDPR, UK Records Act, national learner-rights, retention and credential-authority rules).

decisions.concept: Single-provider waiver: absence of independent Claude and Grok review
decisions.disposition: Required: publication hold must remain active and visible
decisions.rationale: Provider policy requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and a visible absence-of-external-review hold. For WM-ACT-038, Claude Sonnet and Grok 4.6 each timed out on exactly one bounded 120-second attempt. No external result was admitted. This audit is the mandated no-tools review. The internally valid result may be published as a reviewable draft, but it must retain a visible hold pending independent review or explicit owner authorization for canonical promotion.

publicationHolds: Codex single-provider fallback research: Claude Sonnet and Grok 4.6 each timed out on their one bounded 120-second attempt for WM-ACT-038. No external provider result was admitted. The source-grounded Codex fallback passed local schema validation and the required separate no-tools adversarial audit. The result remains reviewable-draft pending independent review or explicit owner authorization for canonical promotion, and this hold must remain visible.

Specification-version verification required before final promotion: Edu-API is Candidate Final Public (not released); Common Cartridge 1.4 is Candidate Final. Accept for draft and peer review; final release requires conformance to final-version standards or explicit specification-level hold declaration in publication artifacts.

Schema-level enforcement of inference safeguards deferred: policy forbids collapsing login into attendance, activity into learning, score into mastery, completion into credit. Data model currently lacks technical constraints (required evidence-method fields, confidence markers, forbidden-inference rules). Publication hold pending schema-level additions that make these distinctions machine-auditable and prevent silent consumer collapse.

Interoperability round-trip not proven: mappings among ISCED, ELM, Edu-API, OneRoster, Caliper, CASE, QTI, xAPI, CLR and CourseInstance are listed as intentional but proposed relations or mapping versions remain held for review. No working mapping tables, version-pair conflict rules or bidirectional validation were supplied. Hold pending approved mapping specifications with identified omissions and conflict resolution.

Regional legal and accessibility variance requires education-sector specialist review: model explicitly acknowledges jurisdiction variation (FERPA, GDPR, UK Records Act, national retention, consent, learner-rights, child protection, intellectual property, credential authority) and regional context assumptions (K-12 vs. higher-education vs. vocational vs. workplace vs. community vs. informal). Known omissions state this review is required before canonical promotion. Hold pending education-sector audit, accessibility conformance assessment, child-protection governance mapping and jurisdiction-specific policy coverage.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.
deferredResearch: Interoperability proof-of-work: develop and approve working test mappings among ISCED, ELM, Edu-API, OneRoster, Caliper, CASE, QTI, xAPI, CLR and CourseInstance with explicitly identified omissions, semantic conflicts and round-trip limits. Include version-pair specific conflict-resolution rules and formal approved mapping tables for each relevant standard pair to move from intentional coverage to validated interoperability.

Schema-level inference-safeguard enforcement: augment data model with required evidence-method enum fields, confidence and source-authority markers, and forbidden-rule validators to prevent silent collapse of login-into-attendance, activity-into-learning, score-into-mastery and completion-into-qualification. Add machine-auditable schema constraints and implement validation rules at model level.

Regional legal and accessibility audit: conduct formal cross-context review spanning K-12, higher-education, vocational, workplace, professional, community and informal learning contexts. Map jurisdiction-specific requirements (FERPA, GDPR, UK Records Act, COPPA, VCAA, regional learner-rights), disability-access conformance (WCAG 2.2 implementation profile by context), child-protection policy, intellectual-property attribution rules and credential-authority delegation governance. Document context-specific profile invariants and version the model accordingly.

Composition-relation artifact schema design: define explicit reference types for person-reference, learner-reference, organization-reference, programme-reference, course-definition-reference, activity-reference, competency-reference, session-reference, location-reference, resource-reference, tool-reference, enrollment-reference, assessment-reference and credential-reference to enforce external-master boundaries at schema level and prevent accidental ownership collapse.

Delivery-form profile invariants: formal cohort courses, self-paced offerings, workplace training, community learning and informal single-activity sessions require different governance rules, completion criteria, assessment authority, credential eligibility and learner-rights protections. Currently a single slash name and mandatory profile attempt to cover all forms. Document mandatory profile variations and develop context-specific schemas or version controls for each delivery form.

model.name: Education / Qualification
model.purpose: Represent a person's source-qualified learning path, assessed outcomes, qualification awards, credentials and recognition decisions independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns learner-programme bindings, progress, outcome and result references, personal awards, credential lifecycle links, transcripts, comparability and recognition assertions, disclosure and provenance. External systems own people, institutions, programmes, courses, teaching, assessments, skills, occupations, licences, payments, immigration, consent and cryptographic proof infrastructure.
in_scope: Education systems, programme and qualification references, learner admission, enrolment, pathway, credit and prior learning
Learning outcomes, assessment evidence, grades, validation, qualification award, conferral and credential lifecycle
Transcripts, portability, comparability, recognition, disclosure, provenance, standards mappings and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Person and institution identity, teaching content and delivery, assessment execution, skills and occupation taxonomy masters

Universal grade, credit, framework, recognition, privacy, retention or minor-learner rules

boundary_notes.distinction: Reusable offerings and teaching execution keep their own masters; this model stores learner bindings, requirements and result links.
Assessment owns instruments, attempts and evaluation execution; the learner record stores evidence references, original result and competent validation effect.
The qualification is reusable, the award is a competent person-specific decision, and the credential is issuer-controlled evidence with an independent status lifecycle.
External taxonomies own concept meaning; education assertions store versioned alignments and demonstrated levels without remastering them.
A qualification can be evidence for a downstream licence or admission decision but never grants that authorization automatically.
Subject identity, access decisions and cryptographic execution remain external; this model records bindings, purpose and evidence.

Learners receive lawful access, portability, correction and disclosure control while registrars and awarding bodies retain source custody and statutory duties.

Validate certified ISCED, framework, ESCO, CTDL, CLR, Open Badges and VC projections with licence, disclosure, mapping-loss and round-trip tests.

bundles.name: Framework, programme and offering
